beats.spoken: In the EU, every claim on a cosmetic has to meet six criteria.
They're set out in Regulation 655 from 2013. The first three are legal compliance, truthfulness and evidential support. So a claim must be allowed, true, and backed by evidence.

Then come honesty, fairness and informed decision-making. A claim can't go beyond the evidence, it can't put down other products, and it has to be clear and understandable. Each claim is judged by how an average, reasonably well-informed consumer would understand it.

items.title: Honesty
items.sub: no more than the evidence shows

beats.spoken: The US has no such list. The Food and Drug Administration doesn't approve cosmetic claims before products go on sale. But it does require labels to be truthful and not misleading.

The annex gives concrete examples. Saying a product has been approved by an authority is not allowed. And if a claim highlights an ingredient, that ingredient has to be deliberately there. And any studies used as evidence have to be relevant to the product and the claimed benefit.
For you, that means three questions for every claim: does it sound true, is there evidence, and do you understand exactly what's being promised?
Check first, then believe. Beauty knowledge, clearly explained: follow Dewlane.
